title: State of the Art
summary: Spaceballs' 1992 Amiga demo won The Party with filmed dancers turned into vector animation.
description: Spaceballs released State of the Art at The Party in December 1992, winning the Amiga demo competition. Filmed dancers were converted into vector animation, with music credited to Travolta and loader music by Vinnie. The production became a memorable example of the Amiga demoscene's combination of programming, graphics and sound.

seo.title: State of the Art (1992) – Spaceballs | Amiga Demo
seo.description: Spaceballs' State of the Art won The Party's 1992 Amiga demo contest, combining vectorised dancers with music by Travolta. Explore the original production.

title: 9 Fingers
summary: Spaceballs followed State of the Art with this two-disk Amiga dance demo at The Party 1993.
description: Spaceballs followed State of the Art with 9 Fingers in December 1993. The two-disk Amiga demo returned to filmed dancers and electronic music, finishing fourth in the demo competition at The Party 1993. Credits include music by Travolta and Vinnie, with graphics and code contributed by members of Spaceballs.

seo.title: 9 Fingers (1993) – Spaceballs | Amiga Demo
seo.description: Watch 9 Fingers by Spaceballs, the two-disk Amiga dance demo released at The Party 1993, featuring filmed dancers and music by Travolta and Vinnie.

title: Jesus on E's
summary: LSD's two-disk 1992 Amiga rave demo, presented at Digital Symposium with music by Echo.
description: LSD presented Jesus on E's at Digital Symposium 1992. This two-disk Amiga production runs through an extended sequence of rave-inspired visuals and tracks composed by Echo. Its length and music-led presentation made it an unusually substantial release for the 1992 demoscene.

seo.title: Jesus on E's (1992) – LSD | Amiga Demo
seo.description: Jesus on E's is LSD's two-disk Amiga rave demo from Digital Symposium 1992, featuring an extended soundtrack composed by Echo. Explore its history.

title: Neverwhere
summary: Crionics won the Bounty Party 1990 demo competition with Neverwhere.
description: Crionics released Neverwhere at Bounty Party 1990, where it took first place in the Amiga demo competition. The production combines code and graphics from the group with music credited to Tronic and S.L.L, reflecting the multi-part megademo approach popular in the early Amiga scene.

seo.title: Neverwhere (1990) – Crionics | Amiga Demo
seo.description: Neverwhere by Crionics won the Amiga demo competition at Bounty Party 1990, with music by Tronic and S.L.L. Discover this early demoscene release.

title: Odyssey
summary: Alcatraz's five-disk-side Odyssey won the Amiga demo competition at The Party 1991.
description: Alcatraz's Odyssey won the Amiga demo competition at The Party 1991. Its five-disk-side presentation follows a sequence of science-fiction settings and story-driven scenes, accompanied by music credited to Greg. Odyssey beat Hardwired into second place at the same event and remains associated with the ambitious trackmo format of the period.

seo.title: Odyssey (1991) – Alcatraz | Amiga Demo
seo.description: Alcatraz's Odyssey won The Party 1991 Amiga demo competition. Explore its five-disk-side science-fiction presentation and music by Greg.

title: Enigma
summary: Phenomena's Enigma won the Anarchy Easter Conference 1991 Amiga demo competition.
description: Phenomena's Enigma won the Amiga demo competition at Anarchy Easter Conference 1991. The release includes ray-traced animation and music by Firefox and Tip, alongside graphics and code from other members of the group. Enigma remains a notable early example of the Amiga's graphics and sound working together in a demo.

seo.title: Enigma (1991) – Phenomena | Amiga Demo
seo.description: Enigma by Phenomena won Anarchy Easter Conference 1991's Amiga demo contest, featuring ray-traced animation and music by Firefox and Tip.

title: Hardwired
summary: Crionics and The Silents placed second at The Party 1991 with this two-disk Amiga demo.
description: Hardwired was a joint release by Crionics and The Silents at The Party 1991, finishing second behind Alcatraz's Odyssey. This two-disk Amiga production features 3D vector effects and music by Jesper Kyd, with programming and artwork contributed by members of both groups.

seo.title: Hardwired (1991) – Crionics & The Silents | Amiga Demo
seo.description: Hardwired by Crionics and The Silents finished second at The Party 1991. Watch the two-disk Amiga demo with 3D effects and music by Jesper Kyd.

title: Sound of Silents
summary: A 1990 Amiga musicdisk by The Silents, featuring compositions by Jesper Kyd.
description: The Silents released the Amiga musicdisk Sound of Silents at Bounty Party 1990. Its soundtrack features work by Jesper Kyd, including pieces titled Apocalypse, Next Decade and Highlands. Rather than concentrating on a single visual effect, the musicdisk gives the group's compositions their own showcase.

seo.title: Sound of Silents (1990) – The Silents | Amiga Musicdisk
seo.description: Sound of Silents is The Silents' 1990 Amiga musicdisk featuring music by Jesper Kyd, including Apocalypse and Next Decade.

title: Desert Dream
summary: Kefrens won The Gathering 1993 with this two-disk Amiga demo and music by Laxity.
description: Kefrens won The Gathering 1993 Amiga demo competition with Desert Dream. Spread across two disk sides, the production brings together 3D scenes, dot landscapes and tunnel effects, with several soundtrack pieces by Laxity. Its mixture of visual techniques and music helped make it a defining 1993 release for the group.

seo.title: Desert Dream (1993) – Kefrens | Amiga Demo
seo.description: Kefrens' Desert Dream won The Gathering 1993 Amiga demo competition, combining 3D effects and dot landscapes with music by Laxity.

title: Follow Me
summary: Red Sector Inc.'s 1989 Amiga demo features a soundtrack by Romeo Knight.
description: Red Sector Inc. released Follow Me in December 1989. The Amiga demo includes coding by Delta and Dr. Beat, graphics by Dark and music by Romeo Knight. It also appeared in early demoscene charts, placing fifth in the EuroChart Top Ten published in March 1990.

seo.title: Follow Me (1989) – Red Sector Inc. | Amiga Demo
seo.description: Follow Me is a 1989 Amiga demo by Red Sector Inc., with code by Delta and Dr. Beat and music by Romeo Knight. Explore its early scene history.
